literature_notes: DAGLA is a four-pass transmembrane protein. Its only extracellular-facing regions are ECL1 (residues 44–60) and ECL2 (residues 121–133). The two ledger entries both describe tags on intracellular termini: L1 reports a C-terminal V5 tag (residue 1042, which lies in the large intracellular domain 155–1042), and L2 reports an N-terminal FLAG tag (residue 1, which lies in the intracellular N-terminus 1–17). Neither ledger line documents any insertion in ECL1, ECL2, or any other extracellular-facing position. Because the ledger is the only permitted source of citations and neither entry supports a surface tag site, zero sites are reported. This is the correct answer, not a failure.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal V5-His tag on full-length DAGLA expressed in pcDNA3.1D/V5-His-TOPO; residue 1042 (R) falls within the large intracellular domain (155–1042), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
N-terminal FLAG tag on full-length DAGLA expressed in pcDNA3.1; residue 1 (M) falls within the intracellular N-terminus (1–17), so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
